newsitem.title: LEBANON: Libano-Francaise issues EuroCDs, raises capital.
newsitem.headline: Libano-Francaise issues EuroCDs, raises capital.

text.p: Shareholders in Beirut's Banque Libano-Francaise approved on Tuesday a $100 million EuroCD issue and a 40 billion Lebanese pounds ($25.2 million) capital increase, a bank executive said.
Maurice Kayrouz, Director of Merchant Banking, told Reuters the annual assembly voted to raise capital to 100 billion from 60 billion.
"Shareholders agreed today to raise capital through the capitalisation of reserves and retained earnings," he said.
Banque Libano-Francaise ranked first among Lebanon's 82 commercial banks in terms of net profits in 1996. It ranked fourth in terms of assets and customer deposits.
Shareholders also approved a $100 million EuroCd issue, the first by the bank, and Kayrouz said the subscription would close by Thursday.
"We feel it is the appropriate vehicle...We enjoy a good standing which would enable us to do it at a low price," he said.
The notes will have five-year maturities and will be priced at between 225 and 245 basis points over equivalent U.S. Treasuries.
"We expect the final spread to be at the lower end," Kayrouz said.
The issue is being lead managed by Indosuez, acting through Indosuez Capital Emerging Markets in London with Credit Suisse First Boston (CSFB) and Merrill Lynch, Kayrouz added.
"Initial indications are that the issue will be extremely oversubscribed. Closing subscription will be by Thursday at the latest if not today," he added.
Lebanese banks have raised a total of $470 million on international debt markets since 1996.
Bankers and economists have said that Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri has urged the country's commercial banks to raise $800 million-$1 billion abroad by mid-1997.
